loci.name: worker-agent-autonomy-reliability-at-scale
loci.one_line: Can a Director spinning up 100+ Worker Agents with minimal human review be production-reliable today, or does current evidence require heavy governance scaffolding (permission scoping, kill-switches, escalation triggers) before that concurrency target is safe?
loci.rationale: Independently surfaced by both analysts as the single highest-relevance locus, pre-validated against contradiction-graph cluster 'autonomy-reliability-fight'. Directly determines whether the whitepaper's core '5,000-person software company' claim is credible as-is or must be reframed around graduated autonomy with explicit governance. Corpus gestures at the resolution but never cashes out the concrete permission-scoping/kill-switch/escalation design.
suggested_searches: graduated autonomy levels permission scoping AI coding agent fleet governance
Berkeley RDI autonomy levels framework multi-agent software engineering
named engineering postmortem AI coding agent production incident 2026 blast radius

loci.name: pentest-autonomy-regression-vs-mandated-cadence
loci.one_line: Industry data shows full autonomous-pentest reliance falling 29%→9% YoY with no compliance framework accepting a fully human-free AI pentest — does the query's ask for a ~90-min autonomous vuln-sweep-with-auto-patch loop match where the field is converging, or does it require a named human-sign-off gate the query didn't ask for?
loci.rationale: The vendors selling autonomous pentest agents are the same sources whose own survey data and risk commentary complicate the full-autonomy claim. The corpus names the regression but never designs around it (what auto-patches vs. what only auto-flags). Directly load-bearing for Pillar 3's literal 90-minute sweep design.
suggested_searches: OWASP Autonomous Penetration Testing Standard APTS 2026 conformance tiers
safe auto-patch vs auto-flag threshold AI vulnerability remediation production case study

loci.name: probabilistic-skill-sequence-prediction-architecture
loci.one_line: What is the concrete architecture for mining an agent's trace history to probabilistically predict and auto-chain the next Skill/tool call in production, given two unreconciled corpus papers (FSM trace-automata vs. speculative pattern-tuple execution) that point different directions?
loci.rationale: Maps directly to Pillar 2's explicit 'probabilistic sequences' ask, flagged thin after wave 1 and only gap-filled late. The corpus has both halves (trace-mining FSM, speculative-execution scheduler) but never bridges them into one actionable architecture — this determines whether the report's Skill-chaining pseudocode is grounded or invented.
suggested_searches: FSM automata agent trace skill prediction vs speculative tool execution combined architecture
Agent Workflow Memory AWM baseline comparison skill chaining

loci.name: agent-skills-context-overhead-magnitude
loci.one_line: Do Agent Skills with progressive disclosure reduce context overhead and token spend as vendor docs claim, or does the corpus's one empirical study show real, budget-relevant overhead that complicates the cost-optimization pillar?
loci.rationale: Pre-validated from contradiction-graph cluster 'skills-overhead-fight'. Both sides agree Skills are net-useful; they disagree on magnitude (negligible vs. material), which Pillar 6's cost model needs pinned down rather than inherited from vendor marketing.
suggested_searches: Agent Skill token overhead benchmark progressive disclosure measured cost

loci.name: consumer-subscription-automation-policy-risk
loci.one_line: If heavy agentic workloads route through flat-rate consumer subscriptions via automation harnesses to beat per-token API costs, what are the vendor ToS, rate-limiting, and account-suspension risks at software-factory scale — an audited absence in the corpus.
loci.rationale: The corpus thoroughly answers the dollar-economics half of Pillar 6's subscription-vs-API ask but is silent on the compliance/viability half (ToS, abuse detection, suspension risk) despite deep-inference search. The report's subscription-automation recommendation is incomplete without flagging this risk explicitly.
suggested_searches: Anthropic Claude Max acceptable use policy automation CLI rate limit enforcement
OpenAI ChatGPT Plus Pro API terms of service automation ban account suspension

loci.name: agent-self-termination-and-idle-cost-economics
loci.one_line: Beyond infra-level VM idle-shutdown (which vendors are explicit is NOT an agent-logic decision), what decision rule should an agent itself use to conclude 'clean scan, no issues, self-archive' — distinguished from a silently-failed scan — and what does idle-vs-always-on actually cost at 100-agent fleet scale?
loci.rationale: Merges two analysts' overlapping convergent loci (cost economics + self-termination decision logic) — both evidenced by the same corpus cluster (Google ADK idle-shutdown, Microsoft Foundry session management, Blaxel sandbox-billing critique). Maps to Pillar 6's explicit 'quietly self-terminate' ask, flagged thin after wave 1. Mostly a synthesis task over already-fetched sources rather than a fetch-heavy one, hence the smaller budget.
suggested_searches: agent self-archive clean health check no issues found self-terminate design pattern

skip_loci.reason: E2B, Sierra Agency, Microsoft Foundry, and Blaxel notes already give qualitative architecture comparisons without a quantified head-to-head gesture to chase. Cost-relevant portion folded into agent-self-termination-and-idle-cost-economics.

OpenAI-Hugging-Face rogue agent breach is a strong case study but its evidentiary role is already core to worker-agent-autonomy-reliability-at-scale; a separate locus would duplicate rather than add a new question.
